text: Go with custom tooling: ccw-owned peer messaging over its HTTP API replaces native SendMessage/ListAgents for ccw sessions and works across containers, nodes and clusters; native Unix-socket messaging is dropped because sockets do not cross nodes, even on RWX CephFS.

Opt-in peers config section, default disabled, zero behaviour change when off; keys enabled, name (default hostname), advertise_url (default http://<hostname>:<server port>), token (required when enabled, normally ${CCW_PEER_TOKEN}, refuse to start without it, never logged, redacted), static (seed list), heartbeat_seconds, max_missed_heartbeats, join_timeout_seconds, max_message_bytes, inbox_max, max_clock_skew_seconds, max_messages_per_minute; ccw serve --peer URL extends the seed list.

Built-ins off when enabled: CLAUDE_CODE_HARBOR_KITE=0 in the session env, permissions.deny SendMessage and ListAgents in the ccw-written settings.json, and the PreToolUse tool gate denies SendMessage/ListAgents with reason 'use mcp__ccw__send_message / mcp__ccw__peers'.

The ccw MCP server gains peers (optional instance filter; sessions of reachable peers excluding the caller, address <instance>/<session id>, plus name and cwd) and send_message ({to, message, notify_when_idle?}; returns msg_id or a clear error: unknown peer, peer unreachable, too large, inbox full, rate limited); both only registered when peers.enabled; main agent only like the command tool; the agent instructions get a short paragraph about them when enabled.

No.. wrapper supports join/leave endpoints. Config/arguments allow to provide static list of peers for discovery. Leave/join happens on container leave/join. Join operation precedes start hook, leave precedes last hook in lifecycle. New hooks exist pre/postJoin and pre/postLeave. Heartbeat keeps reachable agents list up to date.

Peer routes on the target instance, authenticated by the peer token (constant-time compare; server.auth_token not accepted there and the peer token not accepted elsewhere): POST /v1/peers/messages {from, to_session, message, msg_id, notify_when_idle} with 202 queued, 401, 404 unknown session, 413 too large, 429 inbox full; POST /v1/peers/notices with the same auth; plus the join, heartbeat and leave routes; only mounted when enabled; body size capped before parse.

Per-session inbox: an idle session gets the message as a turn now, a busy one as a new turn after the current turn completes (never typed into a busy PTY, never mid-turn), in arrival order, framed as <agent-message from=... msg_id=...> with a line telling the agent to reply with mcp__ccw__send_message; SSE events peer_message_received, peer_message_sent, peer_message_delivered and metrics counters; the EVENT_TYPES pin in tests/test_event_log.py updated.

notify_when_idle: when the turn that handled a message completes, the target ccw POSTs /v1/peers/notices to the sender instance url and the sender ccw delivers it to the sending session as a short <peer-idle-notice from=... msg_id=...> message under the same inbox and delivery rules.
Same-cluster TLS is out of scope for ccw itself (it does not terminate TLS); advertise_url may be https behind an ingress or mesh; the README says so.
Compose example with two ccw services seeded with each other through peers.static (service DNS urls), a shared CCW_PEER_TOKEN, explicit instance names a and b, one image build, no shared volume.

Tests use the fake claude only, only the fake-claude task edits tests/conftest.py, reusing the fake's MCP tool calls; unit tests per module; an in-process test with ccw services on real HTTP ports proving join, listing, send, framed receive, reply, notify_when_idle and leave; a docker two-container integration test (scripts plus a mise task run by mise run test:integration in CI) proving join, listing, messages both ways and leave on stop; real-claude acceptance of the tool schemas is cannotVerify, not a skipped task.

README: setup, addressing, config rows for every new key, every new route and hook documented, trust model (one shared peer token is one trust domain; any holder can push prompts into bypass-mode agents), cross-node use, the TLS note; examples/*.config.yaml are committed symlinks into src/claude_code_wrapper/data/examples.
Follow the repo CLAUDE.md: test-first, uv run, plain ASCII, no em dashes; tasks of about an hour, at most 8 files.

Plan-review hardening: HMAC-SHA256 request signing keyed by the peer token (never sent on the wire) with a clock-skew window (peers.max_clock_skew_seconds, 60) and nonce replay protection on every peer route; notices off the Stop hook path with status delivered|rejected|dropped (rejected and dropped always notify); at-most-once delivery stated in the README; no '.', '..' or leading-dot names; peer I/O never blocks session work or the event loop; inbox re-check and pending re-kick; per-sender rate limit (peers.max_messages_per_minute, 30, 429 rate_limited); one client retry on connection failures with the same msg_id; README trust model for one shared trust domain.
